subject: armadillo
pitch: A nine-banded armadillo trotting along. A shell of overlapping banded plates in dusty pinkish-tan, a pointy snout, tall leathery ears, small beady eyes, sturdy clawed feet and a long armoured tail tapering to a point. A sprinkle of coarse pale hairs pokes out between the bands.
reasoning:
I need to write a single TypeScript module using the SDK, working carefully since I only have partial reference for the API signatures involved—things like part connections, chains, sweeps, sticks, and surface paint/texture functions. I'm planning a simple armadillo model, roughly 0.75m long and 0.3m tall.

Scaling against a real nine-banded armadillo, I'll settle on about 0.9m total length including tail with a shell height around 0.22-0.3m, short legs, and the model facing +Z with the head at the front. For the skeleton, I'm sketching out a hips root joint and a spine chain running from hips to chest, though I'm uncertain about the exact chain API signature and how roles get assigned—I'll guess at passing a role option into the chain call, and fall back to using joints and parts with bone references to minimize risk if that assumption is wrong.

For the shell geometry, I'm planning to build the body as a scaled ellipsoid using sphere geometry with an array scale, then add the characteristic nine bands across the back using segmented shapes in alternating tan tones—trying to figure out whether boxes, cylinders with limited arc angles, or stacked ellipsoid slices would best capture the banded look without overcomplicating the geometry.

Now I'm sketching the band placement: nine overlapping ellipsoid slices spaced along the z-axis to mimic the wrapping bands, plus a head shield and tail rings, and working through how the head and pointed snout would attach using direction/aim parameters on the part function.

I'm adding ears as small flattened spheres on the head, beady eye spheres near the snout tip, and now working out leg structure -- planning shoulder, knee, and ankle joints for each of the four legs, trying to figure out how parent-child relationships work for the joint function.

For legs I'm building cylinder parts between hip and knee joints, oriented by direction, plus small claw cones at each foot angled forward-down. For the tail I'm sketching a chain of points sweeping backward and tapering toward the tip, though I'm unsure of the exact sweep/taper API so I'm considering building it from simpler parts instead.

Writing tail segment code...

For hairs, I'm planning to scatter small pale cones along the shell's band gaps, placing them manually with slight random jitter rather than relying on surface offset hacks.

Now I'm working out the skeleton layout: hips, spine, neck, and head as a joint chain, plus a separate tail chain for the tapering tail. I'm sketching coordinates for the body ellipsoid and the shell bands along its back, figuring out heights relative to the body's top and the legs underneath.

Setting up band colors and spacing...

Now I'm defining the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, then spine, neck, head joints running along the body, plus mirrored leg joints (shoulder/elbow/wrist, hip/knee/ankle) for left and right sides, and a helper function to build each leg segment as a cylinder between two joint positions.

For the tail, I'm laying out a tapering chain of points curving back and down from the hips, then adding banded cylinder segments along that path with radius shrinking from base to tip to give it a natural taper.

I'm also scattering small cone-shaped hairs along the spine using a seeded random generator, varying their x/y/z positions and outward tilt slightly for a natural, uneven look.

Then I'm positioning dark eye spheres, scaled ear shapes, and a forward-pointing snout cone, all anchored to the head bone with appropriate offsets.

Finally I'm adding small claw cones to each foot, angling them slightly forward and downward from the toe positions.

Now I'm placing the foot spheres at the ankle bottoms, then working out the leg joint coordinates for front and hind legs—shoulder, elbow, wrist on the front, and hip, knee, ankle on the hind legs, mirroring left and right across x. I'm keeping the feet just above ground level so they sit naturally, and now figuring out the thickness of the leg cylinders connecting these joints.

I'm writing a helper function to build each leg segment as a cylinder spanning two joint points with the right radius, bone, and orientation, then thinking through how to give the pose a slight trot asymmetry by nudging the front and hind leg positions forward or backward a little. Now I'm settling on the color palette for the model—tan body, darker bands, pale and dark accent hairs, claws, ears, and alternating tail bands—and planning the module structure with the builder import and a default export function that returns the finished root.

Writing joint hierarchy and body geometry...

Defining hind leg joints...

Still defining foot and claw geometry...

Still writing limb helper code...

Now defining tail points with gradually decreasing scale along a curved path for the tail shape.

Adding tail-tip cone and hair placement...

Adding more hair bones...

I'm assuming the rng function returns a callable generator, then adding the exported meta object with name and description, and making sure the feet sit near ground level at y near zero.
